                       Public Utility Commission of Texas

                                          Memorandum


TO:              Interested Persons

FROM:            Jessie Horn, Sr. Counsel, Rules and Projects Division

DATE:            March 23, 2026

RE:              Project No. 58482, Large Load Demand Management Service


         Last year, the Legislature required the Commission to require ERCOT to develop a
reliability service to competitively procure demand reductions from large load customers with a
demand of at least 75 megawatts (MW) to be deployed in the event of an anticipated emergency
condition.1 The rules governing the service must:
       (1) specify the periods when the service may be used to assist with maintaining reliability
           during extreme weather events;
       (2) ensure that ERCOT provides at least a 24-hour notice to large load customers and
           requires each large load to remain curtailed for the duration of the energy emergency
           alert event or until the load can be recalled safely; and
       (3) prohibit participation by any large load customer that curtails in response to the
           wholesale price of electricity, as determined by ERCOT, or that otherwise participates
           in a different reliability or ancillary service.
        Commission Staff requests feedback on two options being considered for implementation
of PURA § 39.170(b). The two options—an as needed service and a seasonal service—and some
trade-offs to each of the two options are described in the slides attached to this memorandum. In
addition to feedback on the two options, Commission Staff requests responses to questions for
comment to assist with drafting a proposed rule to implement the statute and establish a framework
for the Large Load Demand Management program.

        Comments may be filed through the Interchange on the Commission’s website or by
submitting a paper copy to Central Records, Public Utility Commission of Texas, 1701 North
Congress Avenue, P.O. Box 13326, Austin, Texas 78711-3326. Comments are due by April 8,
2026. All comments should reference Project No. 58482. Each set of comments should include
a standalone executive summary as the last page of the filing. This executive summary must be
clearly labeled with the submitting entity’s name and list each substantive recommendation made
in the comments.




       1
           PURA § 39.170(b) as enacted by Senate Bill 6 (89R).
 Commission Staff requests responses to the following questions for public comment:

      1. Of the two options described in the attached slides, an as-needed service or a seasonal
         service, which is the better option to implement PURA § 39.170(b) and why?
      2. PURA § 39.170(b) states the commission must require ERCOT to develop a reliability
         service to be deployed in the event of an anticipated emergency condition. PURA
         § 39.170(b)(1) states the rules governing the new service must specify the periods when
         the service may be used to assist with maintaining reliability during extreme weather
         events.
          a. Does PURA authorize ERCOT to deploy the new service in circumstances other
             than extreme weather events? If yes, what kind of events?
          b. Should the commission define “extreme weather event” and, if so, how should it be
             defined?
      3. PURA § 39.170(b)(3) states the rules governing the new service must prohibit
         participation by any large load customer that curtails in response to the wholesale price
         of electricity, as determined by ERCOT, or that otherwise participates in a different
         reliability or ancillary service. PURA § 37.0561(e)—which allows ERCOT to direct a
         large load customer with onsite backup generation to either curtail its load or deploy
         its backup generation under certain circumstances—states that a large load customer
         with onsite backup generation may participate in a service authorized by PURA
         § 39.170(b).
          a. What type of qualification is necessary to show that it may take a large load
             customer 24 hours to ramp down safely?
          b. What specific prohibitions not enumerated in PURA § 39.170(b), if any, should
             apply to participation in the new service?
          c. Should participation in price responsiveness to transmission scarcity such as four
             coincident peak (4CP) or a successor methodology preclude participation in the
             new service?
          d. Should the commission define “curtailment in response to wholesale price of
             electricity” and, if so, how should it be defined?
      4. How should the target quantity, budget, and price be set for the new service?
      5. What additional information should the Commission consider in its implementation of
         PURA § 39.170(b)?
      6. PURA §39.170(a) states: The commission shall require the independent organization
         certified under Section 39.151 for the ERCOT power region to ensure that each electric
         cooperative, transmission and distribution utility, and municipally owned utility
         serving a transmission-voltage customer develops a protocol, including the installation
         of any necessary equipment or technology before the customer is interconnected, to
         allow the load to be curtailed during firm load shed. The electric cooperative,
                                               2
 transmission and distribution utility, or municipally owned utility shall confer with the
customer to the extent feasible to shed load in a coordinated manner. This subsection
applies only to a load interconnected after December 31, 2025, that is not: (1) Load
operated by a critical load industrial customer, as defined by Section 17.002; or (2)
Designated as a critical natural gas facility under Section 38.074. Should the
Commission include in this rulemaking a directive implementing PURA §39.170(a)?




                                      3
 Proposed Options for Large Load Demand
Management Service

Proposed Options:

Option 1 – “As-Needed”: Procured on an as needed basis just prior to an
extreme event identified by ERCOT. Only offers that have met pre-qualified
requirements will be considered during the procurement process.

Option 2 – Seasonal: Procured on a seasonal basis to be available as an
additional tool during any event during the season as needed by the ERCOT
operator. Any interested resource will need to complete the qualification
requirements in compliance with the seasonal procurement schedule
provided by ERCOT. This process will be similar to the procurement process
for ERS today.
